title: ARWP Trend Radar
goal: Track material Search, AI-search, citation and agent-web changes from primary sources and turn confirmed applicable changes into reviewable ARWP growth actions without promising ranking outcomes.

stageDefinitions.watch: Interesting or emerging mechanism. Keep visible, but do not recommend it by default until applicability and upstream maturity justify adoption.
stageDefinitions.adopt: Primary-source-backed mechanism with a concrete, currently applicable publisher action or measurement path.
stageDefinitions.measured: ARWP has real longitudinal before/after outcome evidence for the linked action. Correlation remains separate from causation.
stageDefinitions.retired: Historical or deprecated mechanism that should not be promoted as a current growth tactic.

trends.title: Treat ChatGPT Search access and ChatGPT Agent accessibility as separate website surfaces
trends.change: OpenAI's publisher/developer guidance separates OAI-SearchBot search discovery from GPTBot training controls, documents ChatGPT referral tagging, and recommends descriptive WAI-ARIA roles, labels and states for ChatGPT Agent in Atlas.
trends.whyItMatters: A site can allow ChatGPT search discovery without making the same training choice, measure attributable referrals, and improve agent interaction through ordinary accessibility semantics rather than AI-only markup.
trends.notes: ARIA guidance is an accessibility and agent-operability recommendation, not a ranking signal.

trends.title: Content-use preferences are becoming operational rather than merely declarative
trends.change: Cloudflare Browser Run's crawl endpoint now enforces the Content Signals `use` directive and can reject requests whose declared intended use exceeds the publisher's allowed level.
trends.whyItMatters: Publisher AI-use policy can affect compatible retrieval tooling at runtime. ARWP should observe and model this without treating one provider convention as a universal web standard.
trends.notes: WATCH by default because this is provider-specific and must not be generalized into Google/OpenAI requirements.

trends.title: Generative Search visibility can be measured as a first-class owner metric
trends.change: Google's Generative AI performance reporting in Search Console is available to websites globally, creating a direct owner-side measurement surface for generative Search exposure.
trends.whyItMatters: ARWP improvements can be followed by explicit before/after observation instead of relying only on crawlability or generic Search traffic proxies.
trends.notes: Measurement availability does not imply ARWP caused any observed movement.

trends.title: Re-review third-party and white-label content under Google's updated site-reputation enforcement
trends.change: Google adjusted its site reputation policy enforcement approach in the EEA while retaining the underlying concern about third-party content published primarily to exploit host reputation.
trends.whyItMatters: Sites expanding content partnerships, directories or sponsored sections should keep those sections aligned with the site's real editorial purpose rather than using domain authority as a distribution shortcut.
trends.notes: This is a policy/compliance review opportunity, not a tactic for increasing rank.

trends.title: Preferred Sources now has a first-party interactive acquisition button
trends.change: Google added instructions for a custom interactive Preferred Sources button that can guide a reader through selecting a publication and then return them to the site.
trends.whyItMatters: For sites with repeat readers, this creates a concrete acquisition surface tied to user preference rather than a generic SEO signal.
trends.notes: User preference may increase prominence for that user; it is not a general ranking guarantee.

trends.title: Measure social and video search visibility beside website visibility
trends.change: Google added Search Console guidance for platform properties covering supported social and video surfaces such as Instagram, TikTok, X and YouTube.
trends.whyItMatters: A brand's Search visibility is increasingly distributed across owned website pages and platform-native content, so content strategy can be measured across both rather than inferred from website sessions alone.
trends.notes: Only apply when the publisher actually operates the relevant platform accounts.

trends.title: Optimize generative Search with useful primary-source content, not GEO cargo cults
trends.change: Google published dedicated generative-Search guidance emphasizing non-commodity content, first-hand value, useful image/video/local/shopping information and existing Search fundamentals while explicitly rejecting a need for special AI-only markup.
trends.whyItMatters: ARWP should prioritize original evidence, entity clarity, crawl/index fundamentals and useful media over speculative AI keywording or special files that Google does not require.
trends.notes: Special AI discovery files may still be useful for non-Google consumers; this trend only constrains Google growth claims.

trends.title: Evaluate WebMCP with real agent tasks instead of static presence checks
trends.change: Chrome's WebMCP guidance describes the feature as an origin-trial/runtime surface and recommends evals that test whether agents understand when and how to call declared tools.
trends.whyItMatters: For interactive sites, runtime task success can become more meaningful than merely publishing a declaration, but current browser support is still experimental and should remain separately evidenced.
trends.notes: WATCH until browser/runtime evidence justifies broader default recommendations.

trends.title: Treat AI citations and grounding queries as measurable publisher outcomes
trends.change: Bing Webmaster Tools AI Performance exposes cited URLs, citation activity and sampled grounding queries across supported Microsoft AI experiences.
trends.whyItMatters: Publishers can inspect which pages are actually reused as sources and which retrieval phrases led to citation, enabling evidence-backed content iteration rather than guessing from rankings alone.
trends.notes: Citation count is not page importance or ranking, and the product remains labeled public preview.

trends.title: Stop treating FAQ markup as a Google rich-result growth tactic
trends.change: Google deprecated FAQ rich results starting May 7, 2026.
trends.whyItMatters: ARWP should keep historical semantic use cases distinct from stale optimization advice and actively prevent deprecated tactics from re-entering generated growth plans.
trends.notes: Retained for historical and anti-cargo-cult checks.
